units.function: Performs the CLI doctor's narrow configuration-file preflight: resolve the selected path, report absence, otherwise delegate parsing and validation to the configuration store and convert thrown failures into a user-facing result.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI health-check leaf -> CLI config store (readConfig, configExists, resolveConfigPath) and -> shared CheckResult type. It does not reach the database, runtime or HTTP service directly; the actual schema and parsing guarantees remain owned by the config-store dependency and must be assessed with that unit.
units.keyDataModels: CheckResult with name/status/message plus optional canRepair and repairHint; an optional caller-supplied config path; no persisted domain entity. Failure identity is carried only by English display text rather than a stable machine code and structured parameters.
units.lifecycle: Resolve path -> test existence -> fail with onboarding hint when absent -> synchronously read/validate via readConfig -> pass when no exception -> catch any thrown value and interpolate it into a failure message. The check performs no repair and has no retry, timeout or side effect of its own.
units.testAssessment: No focused config-check test was found under cli/src. Static TypeScript coverage can catch interface drift, but there is no behavioral regression proof for absent files, custom paths, malformed configuration, non-Error throws, permission failures or information disclosure in propagated errors. Validation depth is delegated to the not-yet-covered config-store unit rather than demonstrated here.
units.designRationale: A small synchronous wrapper keeps doctor orchestration separate from config storage and gives operators an actionable onboarding/configure hint. Catching unknown thrown values prevents the diagnostic command from crashing, but collapsing every failure into one display-string result loses stable failure semantics.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS also needs local/self-hosted deployment diagnostics that distinguish missing, malformed, unreadable and unsafe configuration without starting production services or requiring real credentials.
units.companyOsFit: The narrow leaf-check shape fits a composable doctor command, but Company OS needs a vendor-neutral diagnostic result with stable code, structured parameters, severity, evidence-safe detail and deployment-profile context. Existence/readability is only one check; secret references, file ownership/mode, symlink policy and configuration/profile consistency must have separate canonical checks.
units.responsibilityConflict: No direct human/Agent responsibility conflict. However, free-form propagated exception text is unsuitable as an audit or API contract, and an operator-facing pass must not be interpreted as authorization, identity validity, secret safety or production readiness.

units.securityFindings: The check reveals the resolved config path and directly embeds the caught error text; depending on store/parser and OS errors, this can disclose filesystem layout or sensitive configuration fragments. It does not inspect permissions, ownership, symlink traversal, secret material, environment overrides or deployment-mode invariants. Reuse only the orchestration idea: sanitize detail, return stable codes, keep secrets out of evidence/logs, and split parse validity from security posture and readiness checks.
